passages.title: Water

boxes.q: What does your body need?
When should you have a drink?
Where does it get so hot?
Why does your body need water?
How can you tell you need water?

order: When it is hot, you sweat.
When the sweat dries on your skin, you cool off.
But each time you sweat, you lose some water.
So you need to drink water all day.

passages.title: Should School Start Later?

boxes.q: Who goes to bed late?
What do some doctors want?
boxes.a: They want school for teens to start at 8:30 or later.

boxes.q: When do some kids get up?
Why are teens not tired at ten at night?
boxes.a: your body clock is not the same

boxes.q: How much sleep do teens need?
boxes.a: about nine hours of sleep each night

passages.orderDir: Put these sentences in the order they came in the passage.
order: Many teens go to bed late.
But school starts early.
Doctors say teens need about nine hours of sleep each night.
But a later start is not good for each family.

passages.title: Schools Are Not All the Same

boxes.q: Who do kids in Arizona have for each class?
What do many kids in Mexico wear?
When does a new group of kids come in Mexico?
Where do kids help clean their school?
Why do kids in Japan clean?
boxes.a: this helps them work as a team

boxes.q: How do kids in Arizona get to the next class?
boxes.a: they get up and walk to the next room

passages.orderDir: Put these sentences in the order they came in the passage.
order: In Mexico, many kids wear a uniform to school.
In Japan, kids help clean their school.
Here in Arizona, kids go from class to class.
Each school has its own way.

passages.title: Your Phone

boxes.q: Who has a phone by the time they are 11?
What did Arizona make?
When did Arizona make the law?
Where does your phone stay in many schools?
Why do some teens not sleep?
boxes.a: they look at their phone at night

boxes.q: How long do teens use screens for fun?

passages.orderDir: Put these sentences in the order they came in the passage.
order: A phone can do a lot.
But a phone can take up a lot of time.
In 2025, Arizona made a new law.
Some kids like the new rules.

passages.title: Jobs

boxes.q: Who wants to get a job?
What is a job?
boxes.a: a way to make your own money

boxes.q: When can you start some jobs?
Where could you work at 14?
Why are there rules for kids?
boxes.a: to keep kids safe and in school

boxes.q: How long can you work on a school day?

passages.orderDir: Put these sentences in the order they came in the passage.
order: Some kids want to get a job.
But there are rules, so you cannot work all the time.
At 14, you could work at a store.
But a job can be hard, too.

passages.title: Dating

boxes.q: Who says they have a boyfriend or a girlfriend?
What do they do after school?
Some families want you to wait. Until when?
Where do they sit with each other at lunch?
Why do some families want you to wait?
How can dating help, some families say?
boxes.a: a way to learn how to be kind to the people you like

passages.orderDir: Put these sentences in the order they came in the passage.
order: Some kids in junior high say they have a boyfriend or a girlfriend.
Some families say this is fine.
Other families say you are too young.
Some kids do not want to date at all, and that is fine, too.

passages.title: Homework

boxes.q: Who gives homework?
What is homework?
boxes.a: school work that you do at home

boxes.q: When can you ask about it?
Why do some people say homework is good?
boxes.a: It helps you get ready for a test.

boxes.q: How much homework is fine in junior high?

passages.orderDir: Put these sentences in the order they came in the passage.
order: Many teachers give homework.
Some people say homework is good for you.
Other people say it is too much.
So some schools do not give homework now.

passages.title: A Shorter School Day

boxes.q: Who would have no one to be with their kids?
What do some kids get at school?
boxes.a: their best food of the day

boxes.q: When could you go home?
Where do some schools have school just four days a week?
Why could a short day be good?
boxes.a: kids would not be so tired

boxes.q: How could a short day be bad?

passages.orderDir: Put these sentences in the order they came in the passage.
order: What if school was just four hours a day?
Some people think a short day could be good.
Other people say kids need more time in school, not less.
So what do you think?

passages.title: Your Brain Can Change

boxes.q: Who did a study?
What can change at any age?
Until when will the teen brain get better?
Where were the women in the study?
Why does it get easier?
boxes.a: When you practice, the path gets stronger.

boxes.q: How does your brain learn something new?
boxes.a: your brain makes a new path

order: Scientists did a study with a group of women in India.
For six months, they worked on their reading.
At the end, they could read like a first grader.
Then the scientists looked at their brains.

passages.title: Friends Can Change You

boxes.q: Who can change you?
What did one study look at?
boxes.a: what teens do when their friends are with them

boxes.q: When did teens take more risks?
boxes.a: when their friends were there to see

boxes.q: Why did they take more risks?
boxes.a: They wanted their friends to like them.

boxes.q: How should you pick your friends?

passages.orderDir: Put these sentences in the order they came in the passage.
order: If your friends work hard in school, you may want to work hard, too.
But it can go the other way.
One study looked at what teens do when their friends are with them.
That is why some people say you should pick your friends with care.

passages.title: If You Do Nothing

boxes.q: Who is this a serious problem for?
What happens in the next grade?
When can you come in for help?
Why do some kids think school work does not count?
boxes.a: They move on even if they do not pass their classes.

boxes.q: How can you catch up?
boxes.a: You can ask your teacher for help.

order: But what if you do nothing all year?
When you get to the next grade, the work is harder.
When they fall behind, it gets harder and harder to catch up.
After a while, some of them stop trying.
